name: BQ76200PWR
title: bq76200: high-side N-channel charge/discharge FET driver for 8 V to 75 V battery packs
summary: The bq76200 drives back-to-back N-channel protection FETs in the positive line of a battery pack, so the pack's ground stays continuous with the host. An internal charge pump on an external capacitor (470 nF and up) lifts the gates 9 V to 14 V above the stack; separate enables switch the charge and discharge FETs, another enables a P-channel precharge or predischarge driver, and PMON_EN switches PACK onto a PACKDIV pin so an MCU can read PACK+ through a divider. It runs from 8 V to 75 V with pins rated to 100 V and pairs with the bq76920/30/40 AFEs or an MCU. It comes in a 16-pin TSSOP; BQ76200PWR is the 2000-piece reel.

pins.name: VDDCP
pins.function: Charge pump output. A capacitor goes from this pin to BAT (470 nF nominal); nothing else may draw current from it.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Supply input from the top of the cell stack.

pins.name: CHG_EN
pins.function: Turns the charge FET gate drive on when high. Internal pull-down; ground it when unused.

pins.name: CP_EN
pins.function: Turns the charge pump on when high. Inside the chip it is ORed with CHG_EN and DSG_EN. Internal pull-down; ground it when unused.

pins.name: DSG_EN
pins.function: Turns the discharge FET gate drive on when high. Internal pull-down; ground it when unused.

pins.name: PMON_EN
pins.function: Closes the internal switch from PACK to PACKDIV when high. Internal pull-down; ground it when unused.

pins.name: PCHG_EN
pins.function: Turns the precharge P-channel gate drive on when high. Internal pull-down; ground it when unused.

pins.name: PACKDIV
pins.function: PACK voltage passed through the internal switch, for a resistor divider into an MCU ADC. Leave open when unused.

pins.name: PACK
pins.function: Sense input from the PACK+ terminal.

pins.name: DSG
pins.function: Gate drive for the discharge N-channel FET. Leave open when unused.

pins.name: PCHG
pins.function: Gate drive for the precharge P-channel FET. Leave open when unused.

pins.name: CHG
pins.function: Gate drive for the charge N-channel FET. Leave open when unused.

circuits.title: Simplified schematic
circuits.description: High-side protection for a battery pack. Two N-channel FETs sit back to back in the positive line, drains joined: Q1 (charge) with its source on the cell side and Q2 (discharge) with its source on PACK+. A P-channel FET Q3 with a 1 MΩ series resistor bridges from the cell stack to the joined drains for current-limited precharge. Each N-channel gate has a 10 MΩ resistor to its own source. BAT and PACK each take a 100 Ω / 0.01 µF filter, the 470 nF charge pump capacitor sits between VDDCP and BAT, and the five enables come from an AFE or MCU. PACKDIV feeds a divider Ra/Rb whose midpoint goes to an ADC.

circuits.title: Charge pump capacitor scaled for FETs in parallel
circuits.description: Partial circuit showing several N-channel FETs in parallel in each direction: Q1A and Q1B (charge, sources on the cell side) driven together from CHG, Q2A and Q2B (discharge, sources on PACK+) driven together from DSG, their drains joined in the middle. The larger total gate capacitance is served by raising CVDDCP between VDDCP and BAT. BAT has the 100 Ω / 0.01 µF filter. Only the charge pump, BAT filter and gate drives are wired; the enable inputs, PACK and PACKDIV are left unconnected.

parts.note: scaled to the gate load: 470 nF supports about 30 nF, 2.1 µF about 90 nF

notes: Two FETs per direction stand for any number in parallel.

circuits.title: P-channel FET across the charge FET for precharge
circuits.description: Partial circuit for precharging a deeply discharged stack. P-channel Q3, in series with the current-limiting resistor Rpchg, runs from the cell stack to the joined drains of the charge and discharge FETs, so it bypasses the charge FET Q1. PCHG drives its gate and an MCU drives PCHG_EN. BAT has the 100 Ω / 0.01 µF filter and 470 nF sits between VDDCP and BAT. The other enables, PACK and PACKDIV are left unconnected.

circuits.title: P-channel FET across the discharge FET for predischarge
circuits.description: Partial circuit for bringing up a load with large capacitance. P-channel Q3 and resistor Rpdsg in series run from the joined drains to PACK+, bypassing the discharge FET Q2, so the load side can be charged through a limited current before Q2 turns on. PCHG drives Q3's gate and an MCU drives PCHG_EN. The charge FET Q1 and discharge FET Q2 each have a 10 MΩ gate-source resistor. BAT has the 100 Ω / 0.01 µF filter and 470 nF sits between VDDCP and BAT.

circuits.title: Separate charge and discharge paths
circuits.description: Partial circuit with two positive terminals. A single N-channel FET Q1 (source on the cell side) switches the charge terminal from CHG, and two or more N-channel FETs in parallel, Q2A and Q2B (sources on the discharge terminal), switch the discharge terminal from DSG. This suits packs whose charge current is far below their discharge current. BAT has the 100 Ω / 0.01 µF filter and 470 nF sits between VDDCP and BAT. The enables, PCHG, PACK and PACKDIV are left unconnected.
notes: Two discharge FETs stand for any number in parallel.

circuits.title: Typical application with a bq76940 AFE and an MCU
circuits.description: A 15-series pack monitored by a bq76940 AFE, with the bq76200 moving the protection FETs to the high side. The AFE's CHG and DSG outputs drive CHG_EN and DSG_EN directly; an MCU, powered from the AFE's REGOUT and talking to it over I2C with ALERT on a GPIO, drives CP_EN, PCHG_EN and PMON_EN from GPIOs and reads PACK+ through Ra/Rb on an ADC input. Q1 (charge) and Q2 (discharge) are back-to-back N-channel FETs with 10 MΩ gate-source resistors; P-channel Q3 with a 1 MΩ series resistor and its own 10 MΩ gate-source resistor precharges through the joined drains. BAT and PACK have 100 Ω / 0.01 µF filters, 470 nF sits between VDDCP and BAT, and the current-sense resistor Rsns lies between the cell stack's negative end and PACK-.
notes: The bq76940's own circuit (cell taps through Rc/Cc filters to VC0 to VC15, the Rf/Cf supply filters, thermistors on TS1 to TS3, the SRP/SRN sense filter of two 100 Ω and three 0.1 µF, REGOUT and CAP decoupling and a boot push-button) completes the pack around these terminals.

operation.text: The bq76200 drives N-channel protection FETs placed in the positive line of a battery pack rather than the negative line. With the switches on the high side the pack's ground stays connected to the host whether the FETs are open or closed, so the host can keep talking to the pack's monitor or MCU and read its state after a fault before deciding to reconnect. It adds a P-channel gate driver for a current-limited precharge path and a switch that puts PACK+ onto a pin for measurement.

An internal charge pump builds the gate drive on a capacitor of at least 470 nF from VDDCP to BAT. CP_EN, CHG_EN and DSG_EN are ORed: any one high starts it, and it stops only when all three are low; it is off by default. Once its voltage passes an internal UVLO, about 9 V above VBAT, it counts as on; CHG and DSG then rise with it to the full V(VDDCP) level. If the load is too heavy for the capacitor and the pump never clears UVLO, CHG and DSG stay off. PCHG drives a P-channel FET and needs no charge pump. When switched off, the pump is not pulled down: the capacitor discharges slowly, and a restart before it has emptied takes less than tCPON.

Drive CP_EN from the host and raise it at system start-up, keeping it high in operation. The pump's start-up time then falls inside the system start-up and a FET turns on in tprop plus its rise time. If CP_EN is not used it should be grounded; each turn-on then also waits tCPON for the pump.
If the VDDCP capacitor is open or damaged while CHG_EN or DSG_EN is high, a residual voltage can remain on CHG or DSG that holds the FETs partly on at high RDS(on), which can destroy them.
A probe on VDDCP loads the pump and reads lower than V(VDDCP); a higher-impedance probe disturbs it less.

CHG_EN, DSG_EN, PCHG_EN and PMON_EN each control one output (CHG, DSG, PCHG and the PACKDIV switch), and CP_EN controls the pump. Their thresholds (0.6 V low, 1.2 V high) suit MCU outputs, and they tolerate up to 15 V so an AFE's FET driver outputs can drive them directly; input current must be limited to 5 mA. Each input has an internal pull-down of about 1 MΩ, so an unpowered controller or an open trace leaves CHG, DSG and PCHG off and PACKDIV disconnected.

The device switches its outputs exactly as the inputs command and does not check combinations: CHG_EN and PCHG_EN high together turn on both charge paths at once. Unwanted combinations have to be prevented by the schematic, the AFE or the host firmware.

A suggested split is CP_EN from the MCU, so the pump runs from start-up, and CHG_EN and DSG_EN from the AFE's FET driver outputs, so an AFE with hardware protection (bq76920/30/40) acts on the FETs with the shortest delay.

A deeply discharged pack is first charged at a much lower current, for example C/10, so the cells' passivation layer can recover. PCHG drives a P-channel FET connected across the charge FET, with a series power resistor to set the precharge current; the MCU drives PCHG_EN to enter and leave precharge. Precharge current is commonly 1/20 of normal charge current or less when the charger cannot lower its own current; the limit set by the cell manufacturer governs. Where the charger itself limits current and the stack is above the bq76200's minimum supply, the CHG FET alone can do the precharge, and PCHG is left open.

PCHG can instead drive a P-channel FET in parallel with the discharge FET, through a resistor, to charge a heavily capacitive load before the discharge FET closes. Recovery after a discharge fault often requires the load to be removed, and residual voltage on a large load capacitance would otherwise take a long time to bleed away, delaying recovery.

PMON_EN closes an internal switch of R(PMONFET), about 2.5 kΩ, from PACK to PACKDIV. An external divider on PACKDIV scales PACK+ into an MCU ADC's range, for charger detection or charge control. The divider must keep PACKDIV within its absolute maximum and its current below 500 µA. To save power, enable it only while measuring. Leave PACKDIV open if unused.

NORMAL: the charge pump is running because CP_EN, CHG_EN or DSG_EN is high, and an enabled CHG or DSG output sits at about V(BAT) + V(VDDCP). SHUTDOWN: all three of CP_EN, DSG_EN, CHG_EN low; the device is fully off, its outputs are low and the current into BAT and PACK is 6 µA typical, 9.5 µA maximum (PACK = 0 V, BAT = 8 V).

The electrical figures assume a 10 nF gate load on a 470 nF VDDCP capacitor. More FETs in parallel, larger FETs, and switching CHG and DSG together rather than one after the other all raise the load on the pump. Beyond about 30 nF a larger capacitor is needed. A larger capacitor lengthens pump start-up and a larger gate load lengthens FET switching, so the design should be tested across its full operating range.

CHG and DSG have internal on and off resistances (about 1.1 kΩ and 0.3 kΩ for CHG, 3.5 kΩ and 1 kΩ for DSG). A series gate resistor can be added to slow FET switching. A 10 MΩ gate-source resistor on each FET is recommended; another value changes the pump's load.

When charge current is much smaller than discharge current, the charge and discharge FETs can be put in separate paths to separate terminals, with fewer FETs in parallel on the charge side to save cost.

BAT and PACK are recommended up to 75 V. With the pump on, up to 14 V more sits above BAT or PACK, about 89 V in total. The pins are rated to 100 V, so the worst transient plus the pump voltage sets the highest stack and pack voltage a design can use.

Put CVDDCP and the BAT and PACK RC filters next to the device. Where the board has separate high-current and low-current grounds, connect VSS to the low-current ground to keep noise off the enable inputs; the two grounds join at the cell stack's negative terminal, on the cell side of the sense resistor.

Decide whether the MCU drives CP_EN (strongly recommended, though CHG and DSG work without it if the slower turn-on is acceptable). Size CVDDCP for the number of FETs in parallel and verify it over temperature. If PMON_EN is used, size Ra and Rb for current and ADC range. Wire the rest as in the typical application.
